title: IRM Energy Ltd - 544004 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with volumes at an all-time high of 50.9 MMSCM (up 8% YoY). Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. Industrial PNG volumes were hit by a 9 March 2026 government notification that cut industrial gas allocation to around 80%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the remaining three quarters and says the current margin level will likely moderate.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore

segments.name: Banaskantha (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 48% of Q1 volume and about 46% of profitability; CNG is about 51% of vehicle sales here. Station additions limited to 10-15 in FY27 as the GA is nearing saturation.

segments.name: Fatehgarh Sahib (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 38% of profitability. CNG penetration only 6%; volumes hit by the industrial gas cut linked to the NGT order. Plans for 2 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Diu & Gir Somnath (GA)
segments.commentary: CNG is 60% of vehicle sales; contributed about 8-9% of profitability. Entire commercial segment converted to PNG, with commercial connections now on PNG. Plans for about 5 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Namakkal & Trichy (GA)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM, up 102% YoY from 2.84 MMSCM; contributed about 5% of profitability. FY27 volume guidance 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26); about 15-17 new stations planned; more than 80 TNSTC buses running, with a target of 200+ buses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected at about INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters; management later indicated overall FY27 around INR 7/SCM and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not be sustained.
Revenue growth of about 25% in FY27 guided; management said a safe range is around 20% or more.
Volume growth of 10-12% in FY27, with total volume targeted at about 250 MMSCM by year-end (FY26: 224 MMSCM).
FY27 capex of about INR 250 crore in total (INR 150 crore for Namakkal and Trichy, INR 50 crore each for Banaskantha and Diu & Gir Somnath / Fatehgarh).
Long-term goal of 20-25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
Management said same-level performance as Q1 will not be repeated every quarter; performance will be subdued going forward, though it expects QoQ and YoY improvement.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore; cumulative capex about INR 1,090 crore.
FY27 capex plan about INR 250 crore; management said it will not exceed this, of which INR 150 crore is for Namakkal and Trichy.
CNG stations at 153 as of 30 June 2026 (up 37% YoY), with 564 dispensing points across four GAs.
Station model mix: franchisee (DODO), OMC and company-operated; the company is moving away from daughter booster and LNG-based models toward online stations.
Diu & Gir Somnath: tap-off from GSPL pipeline and hookup with IOC and GAIL in progress; currently drawing LNG from HPCL's Chhara terminal.
demand_pricing: Pricing: Realisations up about 15% YoY and QoQ per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management); management said price hikes are linked to sourcing cost and it will not pass on further hikes now that Brent is cooling.

Sourcing mix in Q1 FY27: APM and NWG about 32-33% (APM 21%, NWG 11%), HPHT about 35%, long-term (Reliance, GAIL and others) about 32%, CBG blending 1%, spot about 1%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%.
HPHT gas at about USD 9/MMBtu versus spot of USD 14-20; industrial volumes benefit from GSPC and Shell long-term contracts running to 2030.
Industrial PNG volumes were hit by the 9 March 2026 notification (about 80% allocation); CNG and domestic/commercial PNG not affected.
Customer base: 86,590 domestic PNG (+13% YoY), 589 commercial (+36% YoY), 228 industrial (+5% YoY).
Management said it is a price taker; competitors and alternative fuel prices are high, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-time items behind the sharp rise in EBITDA per SCM, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-time items; gains came from pricing, gas sourcing and opex optimisation. It guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and how has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: APM+NWG about 32%, HPHT about 35%, long-term about 32%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%; Q4 FY26 APM about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Namakkal and Trichy volumes and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM (up 102% YoY); FY27 target 25-30 MMSCM, towards the upper end, vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and station additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 250 crore; stations to be added: 10-15 in Banaskantha, 15-17 in Namakkal and Trichy, about 5 in Diu & Gir Somnath, 2 in Fatehgarh Sahib.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the NGT order in Fatehgarh Sahib?
qa_highlights.answer: The NGT order (February 2026) has not been enforced by the Punjab pollution board; supply cuts began 9 March. Management expects ramp-up once enforced and says new industries must use natural gas to get consents.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter license fee a concern and how might it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a 2% license fee disclosed in the IPO document, not profit to promoters, worth about INR 20-25 crore for the year and already included in PAT; it cannot promise the rate will stay unchanged.

risks_watch: Sustainability of EBITDA per SCM: management guided INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not hold, versus Q1 at about INR 10/SCM.

Sourcing dependence: HPHT (about 35%) and long-term industrial contracts (GSPC, Shell to 2030) underpin margins; HPHT supply runs only to a stated date and spot exposure is about 1%, so future gas price moves could compress margins.

Industrial PNG volumes: the 9 March 2026 notification capped allocation at about 80%; Fatehgarh Sahib ramp-up depends on Punjab pollution board enforcement of the NGT order, which has not happened yet.

Namakkal and Trichy execution: FY27 volume target of 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26) depends on spot LPG/LNG supply from IOCL, BPCL, Kochi terminal until GAIL and tap-off lines arrive, which management says takes 9-18 months.

Promoter license fee: 2% of revenue paid to promoters, about INR 20-25 crore for the year; management could not promise the rate will remain unchanged, and minority shareholders have raised the question of a ceiling or absolute cap.

Saket, it'll be highly optimistic to say that same performance, as scale up as in Q1, will be repeated every quarter. But it will be definitely subdued going forward, not up to this extent.
We hope and pray, but we can't guarantee 19% always.
As of now, I can't promise you whether this will continue at a reduced rate or same rate or maybe abolished altogether.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on Q1 delivery and FY27 revenue growth but cautious on margins, stating that Q1-level performance will not repeat every quarter and that 19% EBITDA margin cannot be guaranteed. It was evasive on the promoter license fee going forward and on the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT enforcement timeline.
